criteria: all 19 rows in the Oracle diagnostic plan (already a subset of the 81)
paired_dev_plan and prompt_pilot27 rows where identifiable
every connected content component sharing a normalised claim or reference with an excluded row

selection.content_grouping: Connected components share an NFKC-casefold-whitespace-normalised claim or reference. Components touching any exclusion are ineligible.
selection.stratification: Three rows per claim-language x booklet-language x label cell.
selection.grouping: At most two rows per booklet and one row per exact booklet_url plus normalised vote-title group. Among eligible rows, prefer the least represented publication date and booklet before seeded tie-breaking.
selection.inference_blinding: reference_string and label are evaluation-only and must not enter retrieval queries, reranking features or model prompts. The supplied vote title is valid application input, not an inferred gold vote ID.

limitations: This is a genuinely new paired case matrix, but not an independent dataset: earlier full-corpus retrieval work exposed the source dataset.
Exact multilingual vote identity is not available as a reliable source field. Translated titles may describe the same proposal, so booklet/vote grouping reduces but cannot eliminate topic leakage.
Normalised content grouping does not detect every semantic or translated near-duplicate.
Freeze all retrieval weights and model settings before inference; do not tune on these 81 cases.
